utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Would the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-03-69-I, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances. MS. DEL PONTE: For the Prosecution, Prosecutor Carla Del Ponte, senior trial attorney Susan Somers, trial attorney Camille Bibles, and the case manager, Stephanie Wee. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. And for the Defence, please. MR. V. VUKCEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am Vladan Vukcevic, attorney at law. The colleague next to me is Slobodan Vukcevic, attorney at law. And we are going to be the defence team for Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vukcevic. Mr. Stanisic, can you hear the proceeding in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you don't feel well, you may sit down. Would you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And for your identification, would you please state your date and place of your birth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 30th of July 1950, in Ratkovo, in the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it in the region of Vojvodina?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This proceeding is the Initial Appearance of Mr. Jovica Stanisic, pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the International Tribunal. The indictment against the accused and Mr. Franko Simatovic was reviewed and confirmed by a permanent judge of this Tribunal on the 1st of May, 2003. Subsequently, Mr. Simatovic was transferred to this Tribunal on Friday, 30th of May, 2003, upon which the President of this Tribunal assigned the case to the Trial Chamber III. And as one of his permanent Judges, I was designated as the presiding Pre-Trial Judge. And the accused himself was transferred to this Tribunal on Wednesday, 11th of June this year, and I scheduled the present Initial Appearance as the Pre-Trial Judge. First of all, as the Pre-Trial Judge, I have to make certain that the accused understands the indictment against him. Mr. Vukcevic, has your client received the indictment in his own language? MR. V. VUKCEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, he has received the indictment. We are familiar with its contents in detail, and as far as the Defence is concerned, there is no need to have it read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then the next step is then entry of a plea to the charges of the indictment. The accused may either enter a plea within 30 days of the Initial Appearance, but he may enter a plea at the time of the Initial Appearance if he so wishes. Mr. Vukcevic, does your client wish to enter a plea today or do it later? MR. V. VUKCEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, he is going to do it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then I will ask the Registrar to put each count of the indictment to the accused and then the accused will plead. But Mr. Stanisic, could you confine your answer either to guilty or not guilty. Yes, Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 1: Persecutions on political, racial, or religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic, do you plead to count 1 guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm convinced that I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Count 2, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 2: Murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How do you plead, Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm convinced that I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Count 3, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 3: Murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you plead guilty or not guilty to count 3, Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm convinced that I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Count 4, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 4: Deportation, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(d) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How do you plead, Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm convinced that I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Then let's go to the last count.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 5: Inhumane acts (forcible transfer), a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please sit down. I would like to ask the Registrar to note that Mr. Stanisic has pleaded not guilty to all of the counts of the indictment. Then I must now remind the Prosecutor that, pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i), to make available within 30 days to the Defence, in a language which the accused understands, all the supporting materials which accompany the indictment, and also all prior statements obtained by the Prosecution from the accused must be disclosed as well. MS. DEL PONTE: Yes, Your Honour. We will be ready for the disclosure of the supporting material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. Then let me now turn to the Defence, and also tell the Defence that it will have a 30-day period for filing any preliminary motions that it cares to do. Once it has received all of the supporting materials in accordance to Rule 66. Those being said, are there any matters the parties wish to raise at this stage? Nothing from the -- MS. DEL PONTE: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- Prosecution? How about Defence? MR. V. VUKCEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not at this point in time. Nothing special. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic, do you have anything in particular to speak to the Chamber or raise anything, relating to your custody or health, and anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing special to say. Everything that was relevant is what I handed over to the Tribunal through my defence counsel. I am referring to the documents related to my health, and I'm referring to all other matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe the Chamber will be able to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Kwon, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will be able to see the document sooner or later. Yes, please take your seat. And pursuant to Rule 65 ter, the Pre-Trial Judge may be assisted in the performance of his duty by one of the Senior Legal Officers assigned to the Chambers. In this regard, Ms. Yvonne Featherstone, the Senior Legal Officer of our Chamber, shall undertake this task. My understanding is that Ms. Featherstone has already arranged a 65 ter meeting to take place on the 21st of July, together with the Defence team for Mr. Simatovic. Given that Defence has a month's time during which it must receive the supporting material, so the timing seems all right to me. I believe you will be contacted. And then I will have a status conference for the accused and the co-accused, Mr. Simatovic, within approximately four months' time from today. Then this proceeding is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: adjourned at 2.46 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
